coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Channel Pump Station
record.summary: An above-grade wastewater pump station at 455 Berry Street between 6th and 7th Streets, constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010, with a capacity of 103 million gallons per day, which SF Planning's 2020 sea level rise assessment describes as operating continuously in dry and wet weather and conveying flows to the Southeast Treatment Plant.

changes.text: Added a sourced dossier for Channel Pump Station.

The Channel Pump Station record said it was built in 1979, upgraded in 2010, rated 103 million gallons per day and the largest of five combined-sewer pump stations, citing the DataSF Assessor roll and an SF Chronicle article. Neither states any of that, and the article is about Stormwater Pump Station #6, a different building. The record now cites SF Planning's Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, chapter 7, which gives 455 Berry St, constructed 1979, upgraded 2010, 103 mgd, and continuous dry and wet weather operation. The 'largest of five' claim and the sentence about a round, tiled design were removed because no source read supports them for this station. The 1979 milestone now cites the same report.

open_questions: No source read records the construction of the 1979 station beyond the year, or what the 2010 upgrade involved.
The report is dated by its PDF metadata (February 2020); it is the only source read, so the station's current operating state is as described in 2020.
Whether the station sits inside the Mission Bay redevelopment area boundary was not re-checked here; the map note places it in Mission Bay South.

record.notes: Channel Pump Station, 455 Berry St -- an above-grade SFPUC wastewater pump station between 6th and 7th Streets, constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010, with a pumping capacity of 103 million gallons per day, operating continuously in both dry and wet weather; conveys flows through the Channel force main to the Southeast Treatment Plant (source: SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 Wastewater, 2020, which describes it as operating). OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map marks this site 'X1' in its gray/non-developable category; X1 had earlier been left without a record here after an unrelated mislabeling of a street cluster. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 3806006 as 'Industrial Gov Mixed/Other Use' at this address, with no building data on the roll. Status 'existing' (the 2020 SF Planning report above describes the station as operating; not touched by Mission Bay's redevelopment, staying as-is) per this project's own convention for pre-existing infrastructure untouched by redevelopment (e.g. UCSF's own Utilities Plant, Pier 70's Building 21).
